title: Electric mixer
prompt: A labelled teaching cutaway of the page 46 electric hand mixer has two beaters over a bowl. Start drives the motor-shaft worm and the two beater gears so the beaters counter-rotate at a reduced speed. Change speed operates the pictured speed switch and changes motor and beater rates without changing the fixed gear ratio. Stop removes motor power. See-through exposes the motor, worm, two driven gears, beater shafts and shaft-mounted cooling fan. Identify the bowl as a teaching fixture. Do not add an eject mechanism or unsourced electronic controller internals.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Gears and Belts
blurb: A teaching cutaway shows how a motor-shaft worm reduces speed and counter-rotates two beaters over an external bowl fixture.
adaptation: Teaching adaptation, not a literal reconstruction or verified edition union. The bowl is an external fixture. No eject hardware or internal speed-control circuit.
truthNotes: Single-start 24:1 ratio, 1800/3600/5400 example motor rpm, support geometry and dimensions are illustrative; motion is slowed by a factor of ten.
Motor shaft, worm and fan share an angle. Each beater angle is plus or minus that angle divided by 24.
The hand mixer and cord are positioned for a teaching display; a hand holding the mixer and an off-scene mains outlet are omitted.
The source establishes a speed switch but does not establish its internal control circuit.
1988 access restricted and unverified. 1998 page text and 2016 page 46 scan support the retained mechanism. No edition-union claim.
